- **Upgrading from 2026.11.0-alpha.1.** Follow [Upgrade](https://openfief.dev/docs/guides/install/#upgrade) step by step:
  - **Back up the database first.** The core migrates stored data when it starts, and a migration only moves forward. The largest rewrite is `ingest/0015`: ticker confirmations move from each connector instance to its institution (D-153).
  - **SpiceDB now answers authorization by default (D-164).** The install runs the core with `--authz=spicedb`, next to SpiceDB.
  - **Step 5 is required.** Your edited `openfief-db.yaml` must gain this release's SpiceDB `Database` and its `managed` role: diff the old and new database files and copy the changes into your copy before you apply the install. Without them SpiceDB can't start, and the core refuses every authorization check and doesn't become ready; its `/readyz` and its log (`kubectl -n openfief logs deploy/openfief-core`) say what is missing: the role or the database `spicedb` of the `openfief-db` cluster, or the Secret `openfief-spicedb-key`.
  - **To fall back to the policy**, replace `--authz=spicedb` in the core Deployment's args with `--authz=policy`, and pass `--authz=policy` to `core token issue` and `core token revoke` too. The core then answers from its grants table with the same rules, and needs nothing of SpiceDB ([Run without SpiceDB](https://openfief.dev/docs/guides/install/#run-without-spicedb)).
  - **Existing script tokens and view plugins keep reading everything** through a household grant the first core start gives them once, each audited, and writes to SpiceDB (D-209). It shows on the Access page; narrow it there. Grants hold under either `--authz` mode.
  - **New defaults:** each database statement, and each transaction left idle, times out after 2 minutes (`OPENFIEF_DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT`, `OPENFIEF_DB_IDLE_IN_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT`), and each statement of a sync's delivery after 5 minutes (`--sync-delivery-timeout`). Deleting a bond lot now also deletes its coupons and their cash (D-154).
  - **No breaking API change:** `buf breaking` is clean against alpha.1, and no flag or command was removed.
- **Client events, shared cap.** The pages' client-event reports are limited to 30 a minute per address (an IPv6 /64 counts as one address) and 600 a minute for the whole install. Many addresses together can use up the install's minute and hold back legitimate reports until it ends. That trade-off bounds log and metric volume.
- **Plugin metrics.** A view plugin's metric descriptions, scope names and short (64-byte) values of allow-listed attributes reach your OTLP export as the plugin sent them. Install only view plugins you trust with your telemetry.
- **Market quotes.** Quote lookups share an install-wide limit of 60 a minute (10 per caller), so viewers and script tokens can use up the owner's minute.
- **MCP.** Tool calls are not rate-limited per token, except market prices. Every call is audited and limited by the token's grants.
- **Prompt injection.** Text from third parties that reaches the Ask box's tools (instrument names from the market-data provider, statement text from brokers) can try to steer the model. Tools only read, answers are shown only to the asker, and the model can send at most a 32-character ticker-shaped query to the market-data provider.
- **Model spend on your own install.** The daily budget and per-session question limits are off unless set by flags. Viewers you invite can ask the model at your expense. Cap it with the core's flags: `--model-daily-budget-usd=2` refuses model calls for the rest of the day (in the core's `--time-zone`) once the day's calls have cost USD 2, `--ask-questions-per-hour=10` and `--ask-questions-per-day=30` limit each session and each address, and `--ask-concurrent-calls=3` limits calls at once. In your kustomize overlay, add each with a patch of the `openfief-core` Deployment, `op: add`, path `/spec/template/spec/containers/0/args/-` and the flag as the value, for example `--model-daily-budget-usd=2`.
- **The Ask box's conversation lives only in the browser tab (D-224).** It is sent with each question and never stored or logged.
- **Agents and models are off by default (D-212).** One switch in Settings turns them on, with a toggle under it for each of the Ask box's model, the maintainer and the MCP server; an upgrade doesn't turn it on.
- **Client events are on by default and stay local (D-227).** The pages report a fixed set of events (Turnstile's states, script errors, failed requests, the browser's family and version) to your core as log records and metrics; they leave the install only where you set OpenTelemetry export. Turn them off in Settings.
- **SpiceDB's credentials come from a Job (D-216).** The install's Job creates its preshared key and its database role's password only if their Secrets are missing, and never changes or rotates one, so credentials you made yourself stay.
- **Opinions and draft theses are off by default and only for the owner (D-225, D-229).** Turned on in Settings, the Ask box's model may say whether it would buy, sell or hold and why, and suggest a thesis you can save as a draft that only you can read; it never acts, and a draft has no size. They work only for your own session, on a core that runs no demo, and on a route allowed for all three data tiers. Their eval set isn't approved yet, so with opinions on, every answer names its model as not evaluated for opinions, whatever its Ask box verdict, until that model and host pass the opinions set.
- **The eval results page exists (D-222).** The docs' Ask box evaluation results list each model and host with its verdict, failing cases, reliability, cost and run dates; an Ask box answer links to it.
- One delivery from a connector holds at most 200 000 prices (D-190). A longer history doesn't arrive in this release; paged deliveries, each imported on its own, come in a later one.
- Reporting in a currency other than PLN is refused (T-12).
- This is an alpha: contracts may change between releases, while the data already stored is migrated with each change (D-161).
